 Savar journalist Nadim Hossain dies during dengue treatment at 40
 Colleagues mourn the longtime correspondent and Press Club leader after his condition deteriorated rapidly 
 Published : 6 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 6 November 2026, 23:12
 • 
 OBITUARY
 SHARE 
 Our Correspondent, Savar 
 A journalist died of dengue at Enam Medical College Hospital in Savar Friday afternoon while undergoing treatment.
 According to his colleagues, Nadim Hossain, 40, was admitted to the hospital on Wednesday after contracting dengue. As his condition deteriorated early Friday, he was shifted to the intensive care unit (ICU). He was later put on life support as his condition worsened. Doctors declared him dead at 4:36pm.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Nadim lived with his parents in Savar’s Shahibagh area. He had worked for various media outlets for more than a decade.
 He worked as Savar correspondent for Mohona Television, Bangla Mail 24, Bangla Tribune and Dhaka Tribune. He was also the joint general secretary of Savar Press Club.
 Savar Press Club President Nazmul Huda said Nadim was a promising journalist with strong organisational skills.
 "His death is an irreparable loss to journalism in Savar. We extend our condolences and sympathies to his family and pray for the salvation of his departed soul," he said.
 Speaking in the evening, journalist and Nadim’s colleague Noman Mahmud said the first namaz-e-janaza was held in front of Savar Press Club at around 8:15pm.
 The body was being taken to his village home in Singair upazila of Manikganj, where he would be buried following another funeral prayer, he added.
 Meanwhile, Savar Press Club, Dhamrai Reporters Club and other local journalists’ organisations expressed deep sorrow over Nadim’s death.
